title: Edit Binding Properties
content: **List of Contents** Binding Properties Edit Binding Properties **Binding Properties** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vonEOlpfYzQ \- Adjust properties for Binidngs. ** ** \- Select the ![edit_binding.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001829187/edit_binding.jpg)**Select Binding** tool from the 3D toolbar. **※****Note: ** Binding can also be selected with the Select/Move tool from the 3D toolbar. ** Edit Binding Properties** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkwZzbESthw \- When the Binding tool is selected, the 3D garment turns translucent and segments with Binding appear in grey. \- Select the Binding to be edited. \- Selected Binding’s properties appear in the Property Editor. * Name : Rename Binding’s name. * Type: Place the Binding below or above the Pattern. * Line Length: Check Binding’s length. However, it cannot be changed from the Property Editor. * Width (mm): Adjust selected Binding’s width (1~30mm). * Length (%): Adjust selected Binding's length with percentage (50~200%) (ver5.0.0.) * Length (in): Adjust selected Binding's length with a specific value. When adjusting the Binding with a specific value, the unit follows the program's default unit (ver5.0.0.) * Particle Distance (mm): Edit selected Binding’s Particle Distance (1~20mm). * Add'l Thickness - Collision (mm): Adjust the **Add'l Thickness - Collision** value of each Binding (ver5.0.0.) * Fabric: Assign Fabric to the Binding. * Fabric styles in the Fabric Object Browser appear in a list. * Topstitch: Apply Topstitch on top of the Binding. All Topstitch styles added in the Object Browser appear as options (ver4.2.0.) * Sewing Line Type: Edit Binding’s Sewing Line Type. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: "Explore the essential guide to editing binding properties in your 3D garment design, complete with instructional videos and detailed adjustments for optimal customization."

title: Elastic
content: ### List of Contents Pattern Pattern Outline or Internal Line ### Objective Apply elastic to the patterns or lines to express details such as E-bands or shirring. ### Operation #### **Pattern (ver 7.2)** 1. In the Library window, click Fabric » Elastic folder. 2. In the fabric tab of the Object Browser, select the fabric of the pattern to represent E-band. → Property Editor appears. 3. Click the Elastic option on the right side of the Physical Property. → Elastic properties appear. 4. Adjust the Elastic properties. | Preset | Set the default elastic presets. ---|--- Strength and Stiffness | Adjust the strength and stiffness of the elastic. Thickness | Set the thickness of the elastic. #### **Pattern Outline or Internal Line** 1. Select a outer or internal line with ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005538548/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png)**Edit Pattern** tool. → Property Editor appears. 2. Click the Elastic option to **On**. 3. Adjust the Elastic properties. Strength | Adjust the strength of the elastic. ---|--- Ratio | Adjust the ratio of the elastic. Segment Length | Adjusts the elastic ratio when the length value is entered. Total Length | If multiple segments are selected, the entered value will be applied as the total length of the combined segments.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for applying elastic properties to patterns and lines in order to enhance design details such as E-bands and shirring in your fabric projects.

title: Opacity
content: **Opacity** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vi7yKxvRnBk \- Adjust the **Opacity** to express see-through materials. \- Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and adjust Material ▶ **Opacity.** \- Adjust the scrollbar or type in desired values to edit the Opacity values. \- The material’s Opacity will change according to the setting.
content_description: Learn how to adjust the opacity of materials in your project to create realistic see-through effects using our step-by-step guide.

title: Adjust Bending-Weft/Warp
content: ### **Objective** Use **Bending** intensity which is the resistant against being bent, to adjust the stiffness of fabric. The higher the value, the stiffer it becomes such as denim and leather, and the lower the value, the more it becomes suitable for draping materials such as silk. The Bending intensity for the weft and warp directions can be set separately likewise the real fabrics. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ **Bending-Weft** /**Warp** **Expressing materials with Weft (Horizontal) bending intensity** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005548248/________01.png) **Expressing materials with Warp (Vertical) bending intensity** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005548268/________02.png) **※Note:** Adjust Bending for bias by using **Bending - Bias** (ver.5.1.0).
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting fabric stiffness through Bending intensity settings for both weft and warp directions, allowing users to replicate the characteristics of various materials, from rigid denim to flowing silk.

title: Open Textures in AI / PS (ver 6.1)
content: ### **Objective** Open the texture image applied to fabric or trim in Adobe Illustrator/Photoshop. ### **Location** Fabric Property ▶ ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900008317346/mceclip0.png) button right to each map. ### **Operation** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. → The pop-up menu appears. 2. Click Add Another App menu. → Select Application window appears. 3. Select the executable file (EXE) of the application to be added. Click Open button. → The texture will then open in that application and the application will be added to the list of the pop-up menu as well. 4. Save the edited texture in the application, return to CLO, then right-click on the background in the 3D window. ▶ Click **Refresh Textures (F5)**. → The edited texture image appears. **※Note:** * Once you click Open with Another App menu, you can only execute the selected application without adding it to the pop-up menu. * User Settings ▶ [Other](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/360001547188-%EA%B8%B0%ED%83%80-%EC%84%A4%EC%A0%95) you can register or delete the application that is opening textures.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for opening and editing texture images applied to fabric or trim in Adobe Illustrator or Photoshop within CLO 3D.

Rendering thickness from the center of the Garment is set for 0.5mm as default vale, and it is adjustable. This thickness value is only visible and does not Simulate as the thickness value space out between Fabrics. **※ Note: **To see the rendering thickness, 3D Garment Rendering Style must be set on **Thick Textured Surface** . **Location** **Fabric Unit ** Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶ Fabric Item ▶Property Editor ▶ **Thickness** **Pattern Unit**(ver2.3.0) Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Add'l Thickness-Rendering** **Operation** **Fabric Unit** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: ** **Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶ Fabric Item ▶Property Editor ▶**Thickness** 2. Enter desired rendering thickness value. →The thickness is now being adjusted and applied. **Pattern Unit**(ver2.3.0) 1. title: Adjust Buckling Ratio
content: **Objective** Use this function to reflect the tendency of Fabric trying to preserve its shape then being bent when applying certain amount of force. The closer the Buckling Ratio gets to 100 percent (%), the more it becomes easily bendable fabric such as silk and jersey. On the other hand, the closer the ration gets to 0 percent (%), the more it becomes less bendable fabric such as denim and wool. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ **Buckling Ratio** ![_____________.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115018758847/_____________.png) **※Note:** Adjust Buckling Ratio for bias by using **Buckling Ratio - Bias** (ver.5.1.0).
content_description: Explore the Buckling Ratio in the Fabric Property Editor to understand how different fabrics respond to bending forces, with higher ratios indicating more flexible materials like silk and lower ratios signifying stiffer fabrics like denim.

title: Adjust Buckling Stiffness
content: **Objective** Adjust how much percentage (%) of total Bending intensity to use to decide the Buckling Stiffness of the corners of Fabric. This is used alongside Bending-Weft/Warp. For instance, entering a Buckling Stiffness of 80 when Bending value is 60, is going to result in the Bending value of the actual intensity of the part of the Fabric being folded being 80% of 60 which is 48. In other words, the higher the Buckling ratio, the harder it is to fold the corners of fabric, and on the other hand, the lower the the ratio, the easier it folds. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ **Buckling Stiffness-Weft** /**Warp** ** ** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005756128/____.png) **※Note:** Adjust Buckling Stiffness for bias by using **Buckling Stiffness - Bias** (ver.5.1.0).
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the percentage of total bending intensity to determine the buckling stiffness of fabric corners, influencing their foldability based on the specified bending values.

title: [Mode] Emulator
content: ### **Objective** Digitize new fabric and save as a file in Emulator Mode. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Change the mode at the top-right corner ▶ **EMULATOR** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Change the mode at the top-right corner ▶ **EMULATOR** → Emulator window appears. 2. Input the property value of the fabric measured step by step according to the description on the left screen. **※ Note:** Select **Enter All Values** to skip to the last page where users may manually enter all values without going through previous steps. (ver 5.1.0) ![emulator.JPG](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360039474014/emulator.JPG) 3. Press **Compute** once finish putting the value and wait until automatic calculation for the fabric property is completed. 4. Save the calculated fabric as .zfab file. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000708348/1.PNG)
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for digitizing new fabric and saving it as a .zfab file in Emulator Mode.

title: Select Binding
content: ### **Objective** Edit Binding Properties. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Binding ▶ **Select Binding** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Select Binding ** **※Note:** 3D toolbar ▶ Select bindings with the Select/Move tool. ** Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated.** **→ The line segment for which the binding was created is displayed. 2. Select the Binding to be edited. → Its properties appear in the Property Editor. 3. Configure each property as needed referring to below table. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Name** | Rename Binding's name. **Line Length** | Check Binding's length. However, it cannot be changed from the Property Editor. **Type**** ** | **Under** | Bindings are placed under the Patterns to express Inside Bindings. **Over ** | Bindings are placed over the Patterns. **Both (ver 7.0)** | Bindings are placed both direction of the Patterns. **Dimension** | **Width** | Adjust selected Binding's width. (1~50mm) **Length ** | Adjust selected Binding's length with percentage (50% ~ 200%) or a specific value. **Particle Distance** | Edit selected Binding's [Particle Distance](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000414447-Particle-Distance-Setting-) (4~20mm) **Add'l Thickness - Collision** | Adjust Binding's[ Add'l Thickness - Collision](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002798068-Adjust-Collision-Thickness). **Fabric** | Assign Fabric to the Binding. Fabric styles in the [Fabric Object Browser](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/sections/115000714287-FABRIC) appear in a list. **Grain Direction**** ** | Bias/ Warp/ Custom | Choose among Bias, Warp, or Custom for the Binding's grain direction. Angle | Manually insert Angle value to set the Binding's grain direction. **Topstitch ** | Add Topstitch to the Binding. The Topstitch option shows the styles which are added in the Topstitch tab of Object Browser. [**Sewing Line Type**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000496627--Property-Sewing-Line-Type) | Edit Binding's Sewing Line Type. **Extend ** | Set whether to extend the binding after creating it on a part of the line segment. **※ Note:** Binding Extension is not possible in the following cases. When the angle of both segments are more than 180 degrees based on the binding start/end point. 4. Right-click on the Binding to be edited. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Delete** | Delete selected Binding. **Reset Arrangement** | Reset Binding's position. Use this option to fix unstable simulations. **Deactivate / Activate** | Deactivate or activate selected Binding. **Freeze / Unfreeze** | Freeze or unfreeze selected Binding. **Flip Normal ** | The selected Binding's face flips to the other side.
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for editing binding properties in the 3D toolbar, including selection, configuration, and management of bindings within the materials menu.

Color Palette** \- Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material > **Color.** \- The Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for managing color palettes and swatches in design software, offering instructions on importing, creating, modifying, and saving custom color palettes for an enhanced design experience.

title: Refresh Texture
content: ### **Objective** Edit texture images with an image editing tool (Photoshop, Illustrator…) and save over the original image with the same name and file location, press **Refresh** button to instantly apply the changes of the Fabric's texture images. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 3D/2D Window Background Right-click Pop-up Menu ▶ **Refresh Textures**
content_description: This webpage provides instructions for editing and refreshing texture images in the 3D/2D window of a design tool, ensuring instant application of changes.

title: Edit Texture Size (Property Editor)
content: ### **Objective** Use the Property Editor to resize the texture applied to the Patterns. ** Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Fabric (Select the Desired One) ▶ **Property Editor** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Fabric (Select the Desired One) ▶ **Property Editor** → The selected Fabric's properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Find the **Transformation** option which only appears [when a texture is applied to a Pattern.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000471388-%EC%9B%90%EB%8B%A8-%ED%85%8D%EC%8A%A4%EC%B2%98-%EB%84%A3%EA%B8%B0) **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Angle** | Type in the rotating angle. **Width** | Set the texture width. **% (ver5.0.0)** | Configure the texture width with percentage. **Height** | Set the texture height. **% (ver5.0.0)** | Configure the texture height with percentage. **Lock Aspect Ratio** | Lock the width and height ratio.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for resizing textures applied to patterns using the Property Editor in the Object Browser.

title: Unified Map 6.1
content: **Objective** When a pattern construction constrains a print layout, apply the texture using Unified Map. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eqeB6edmo5A **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ On the right button of Fabric Item **Texture Repeat / Unified Map**. Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Material ▶**Texture Mapping** **Operation** 1. Click the tool/ menu indicated. 2. Use Unified Map to apply the texture differently. 3. Set the specific options of the Unified Map. Repeat U | Set the range for the image to be arranged between 0-1 in the U direction. ---|--- Repeat V | Set the range for the image to be arranged between 0-1 in the V direction. **※Note:** Once you have applied the Unified Fabric Map, the Edit Texture Tool will only rotate the Grain-line, NOT the Texture.

title: Import AxF file
content: ### Objective Express textures by using the AxF file of X-Rite that express realistic fabric materials with various maps extracted by three-dimensional scanning of fabric. **Location** Object Browser ▶ **Fabric** **Operation** 1. Click the tool/ menu indicated in Location. ** ** 2. Right click the fabric item and **Import/ Import (Add).** → **Open File** window appears. 3. Select the AxF file and click **Open**. → Fabric property is converted into the property of AxF file. → When using **Import (Add)** , the properties that have already set are retained, only the properties that are not present are changed to the corresponding Axf file. (Ex: When having texture only, the other maps are applied such as Normal, Alpha, or etc) **※ Note:** You can drag and drop the AxF file to **Fabric** in **Object Browser** , 2D Pattern, and 3D Garment.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to importing X-Rite AxF files for realistic fabric textures, enhancing your design with accurately scanned material properties.

title: Specular Color
content: **List of Contents** Specular Color Apply Specular Color Adjust Shininess **Specular Color ** \- The **Specular Color** is the color of the light directly reflected from the fabric used to express glossy materials such as enamel. ** Apply Specular Color** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cYcwPAlf7SA \- Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and select the color chip next to the Material ▶**Specular Color.** \- When the color window appears, select the desired Specular Color. \- Brighter the Specular Color is, glossier the fabric will become. **Adjust Shininess** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6fxPbAKlpRc \- Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and expand the Material ▶ **Specular Color** to see its child menus. Locate the **Shininess** option. \- Move the scroll bar to adjust the gloss of the fabric. Higher the Shininess value is, glossier the fabric will become, like enamel. However, on the contrast, lower the Shininess value is, more regularly the gloss will spread on the surface of the fabric, like lame. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on applying and adjusting specular color and shininess to fabrics, enhancing their glossy appearance through detailed instructions and instructional videos.

title: Adjust Internal Damping
content: ### **Objective** Use this function to set resistance against the bouncing speed of Garments. Increasing the Internal Damping value is going to cause the Garment to slow down as if it is in underwater, and lowering the value is going to cause it to bounce very quickly. **※ Note:** Adjusting the measurement while putting Garments on does not make a noticeable difference therefore it is better to use during animation as it influences Garments when they are moving. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ **Internal Damping**
content_description: This webpage provides guidance on adjusting the Internal Damping value to control the bouncing speed of garments in animations for more realistic movement.

title: Fabric_Normal Map
content: **Normal Map ** * **Normal Map ** \- Apply Normal Map images to express uneven texture more realistically. * **Adjust Intensity YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=otz3z18Sogk -**Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and expand the Material ▶ Texture to see its child menus. Then, expand the **Normal Map** option as well. \- Adjust the intensity of the Normal Map using the **Intensity** option. \- When the Normal Map Intensity values is adjusted from 0, CLO will automatically create a Normal Map and express the texture more realistically. * **Apply Normal Map Images YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XuJC92Ksg1w ** * **Via Property Editor** \- The custom made Normal Maps can be applied to the fabric items as well. \- Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and expand the Material ▶**** Texture to see its child Menus. \- Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022233407/mceclip0.png)icon next to the Normal Map. The Open File browser will appear. \- Locate the desired Normal Map image and click Open. \- Adjust the intensity values to express the texture more realistically. * **Via Drag & Drop \- **From the PC’s Browser window, drag and drop a Normal Map image to the Browser button next to the Normal Map option. * **Apply with Desired Map Type YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ka8kOCuOpGM ****-** From the PC’s Browser window, drag and drop an image file to an object where the image should be applied to. \- The Texture Map Type window appears. Choose the desired Map type and select OK. * Save Auto-generated Normal Map YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=35_-fG1DxC4 \- Normal Map generated when adjusting Intensity can now be saved. \- Adjust the Intensity under the Normal Map option. \- Navigate to Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save as ▶Surface Textures and locate the saving path. \- Select Original size or Crop size when saving. \- The Normal Map can be saved when exporting as OBJ,FBX,LXO. **※** Note: Normal Map and Roughness Map are retained even if Texture is deleted.(ver.4.2)
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for applying and adjusting Normal Map images to enhance the realistic texture of fabric items in CLO software.

title: Texture Generator (ver 7.1)
content: **List of Contents** **Open Texture ** **Select Area of Texture** **Set Options** **Save Texture Image** **Apply Texture** **Objective** Seamlessly generate texture maps with scanned or captured images, and check the results in real-time within the 3D window. **Location**** ** Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶ ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/13169546878617) Texture Generator **Operation ** **Open Texture** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. → Texture Generator Opens. 2. Click Open at the left bottom of Texture Generator to open the texture image. → The size and resolution of the textures loaded are displayed at the top. → For XTEX files, other maps (Normal map, Opacity map etc.) in the folder are automatically loaded. **Select Area of Texture** 1. Find and click on the minimum area where the fabric pattern repeats. ▶ Drag to select. → The optimized result analyzed within the selected area will show up. → The analyzed result is repeated in the preview window at the bottom. 2. To adjust the area, move the point of the selected area. → It is analyzed automatically again within the selected area. 3. To maintain the selected area, click Manual at the right bottom of the selected area. → The selected area is maintained and repeated. **Set Options** The options below can be set only in Auto mode since they work based on the analyzed results. * **Fabric Type ** Select fabric type for more accurate analysis. The analysis is based on Normal Map, thus it is only vaild with the existence of Normal Map. \- Plain: Solid fabric without repeated patterns. \- Repeat Pattern: Fabric pattern is regular. \- Random Color Pattern: Fabric pattern is irregular. * **Equalize ** Adjust the value to equalize the difference in brightness caused by crease in the fabric. ※ Note: Depending on the fabric, some colors or patterns may be distorted. Refer to the attached image. below. ![seamless_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/13171432946713) * **Smooth ** When the connected part of the fabrics are not smooth by crease in the fabric, align weave areas equally. ![image-20221201-064052.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/13171781957657) * **Show/Hide Grid ** Click Show/Hide icon in Preview window at the bottom to check the grid of the repeated texture. **Save Texture Image** 1. Click Save at the bottom to save the generated texture as Image file. → Save Textures window appears. 2. Select the textures and map type to save and click OK button. → Each map name is automatically applied after the set name and saved as PNG files. **Apply Texture** 1. When the texture generating is complete, click the Apply & Close button at the bottom right of Texture Generator. → The texture is applied to the fabric simultaneously and the Texture generator is closed.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a comprehensive guide for seamlessly generating, customizing, and applying texture maps using scanned images within a 3D environment.

title: Express Silk, Velvet and Glass Materials
content: **Express Silk, Velvet and Glass Materials** Express Silk, Velvet and Glass Materials Express Silk Express Velvet Express Glass **Express Silk, Velvet and Glass Materials** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zz7eOW8nVcM \- Express fabric or other objects as silk, velvet, and glass. \- Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶ Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ **Type**. **Express Silk** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZD4_gri0CJM \- Select the object to be edited in the Object Browser. \- In the Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ **Type** , select Fabric_Silk/Satin. \- The selected object is expressed in silk material in the 3D window. **Express Velvet** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FFHNMGbArd0 \- Select the object to be edited in the Object Browser. \- In the Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ **Type** , select Fabric_Velvet. \- The selected object is expressed in velvet material in the 3D window. **Express Glass** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5T4DUYuTZ28 \- Select the object to be edited in the Object Browser. \- In the Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ **Type** , select Glass. \- The selected object is expressed in glass material in the 3D window. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Explore the process of expressing objects in stunning silk, velvet, and glass materials through our comprehensive guides and tutorial videos.

title: glTF a Standard Fabric File Compatibility (ver 6.1)
content: **List of Contents** **Export ** **Import** ### Objective Import or export PBR material and the CLO's physical property as a glTF file. ### Operation **Export** 1. Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Click Fabric (GLTF/GLB) menu. → Save File window appears. 2. Set the file saving path and name then click OK. → Export gLTF window appears. 3. Set the fabric you want to export and format then click OK. → The selected fabric is exported as a glTF or GLB file. **※ Note:** * Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ You can also right-click on fabric items and **Export (GLTF/GLB)** menu. * It's not possible to export the fabric with Substance (SBSAR) material due to the license issue. **Import** 1. Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ Click GLTF / GLB menu. or drag and drop the file in the 3D / 2D window. → Import window appears. 2. Change the type of object to **Fabric** and click OK. → Import Fabric window appears. 3. Select the desired fabric and click OK. → The fabric is added to the Fabric Tab in the Object Browser. **※ Note:** You can also drag and drop a GLTF/GLB file in the fabric item or the fabric tab in the Object Browser. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for importing and exporting PBR materials and CLO's physical properties as glTF or GLB files.

title: Fabric List Window
content: Default_Fabric is provided as default Fabric, and being displayed in the Fabric list. When editing Default_Fabric, the edited default Fabric maintains until reopen a garment or rerun a program. It is able to reset edited properties of Default_Fabric at right-click pop-up menu.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide information on managing Default_Fabric settings, including editing, saving changes, and resetting properties within the garment design interface.

title: Reset Fabric Property
content: ### **Objective** Reset a Fabric in order to return to a default Fabric properties. **Location** 2D Pattern Window ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001074948/_______3D___.png) Edit Texture (2D) ▶ Right-click Pattern Pop-up Menu ▶ **Reset to Basic Fabric** Object Browser ▶ Right-click Fabric List Pop-up Menu ▶ **Reset** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Pattern Window ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001074948/_______3D___.png) Edit Texture(2D)**▶** Right-click Pattern Pop-up Menu ▶ **Reset to Basic Fabric** Object Browser ▶ Right-click Fabric List Pop-up Menu ▶ **Reset** →The selected Fabric's texture, color and physical properties are now being reset.
content_description: This page provides a step-by-step guide for resetting a Fabric to its default properties using the 2D Pattern Window and Object Browser in the Clo3D software.

title: Fabric Information
content: ### **Objective** Enter information of fabric. **Location** [Object Browser](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000374247-%EB%AC%BC%EC%B2%B4%EC%B0%BD-Object-Browser-) ▶ Fabric Tab ### **Operation ** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. 2. Select a fabric item. → The properties appear in the Property Editor. 3. Refer to the table below and enter the information ** Information (ver 6.1) ** | Click the ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4405487275417/mceclip0.png) button to the right of the information menu to check the revision history of the fabric file. ---|--- ** Name ** | Enter the name of the fabric. The name is also reflected to the Fabric List. **Item No. ** | Enter the Item No. of the fabric. ** Classification ** | Type in the content and classification. **Supplier/** **Owner (ver 6.0)** | The supplier and owner entered during fabric creation in Emulator mode are displayed. ** ****※Note:** Such fabric information can be previewed in the Library.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for entering and managing fabric information in the Object Browser's Fabric Tab.
